title: Method for the determination of parameters in the sintering process of mixtures of the elemental powders Fe-Cr and Fe-Cr-Ni
author: Schneider, Biehl, et al.
materials: 5 – After the compaction process, the samples should be identified and conducted to the sintering process. The sintering of the components needs to occur in a furnace with heating capacity of 1200 °C under argon atmosphere. The furnace should be programmed to heat up to the sintering temperature when it is already inert with argon. When the temperature is reached, the parts must be inserted into the furnace. To avoid oxidation at high temperatures, the samples should be placed on an ASTM 304 steel plate with similar chromium content, to avoid high temperature corrosion or the segregation of components [2]. The gas should be leaked at 4 l/min. The heating rate needs to be measured by positioning an auxiliary thermocouple right above the samples, controlled by a thermometer with a minimum resolution of 0,1 °C and referenced at 1200 °C, according to the calibration certificate. The time taken for the samples to reach the final temperature must be observed, and then the samples should be kept in the furnace for 60, 180 and 360 min. After the specified time has been taken, the parts should be removed from the furnace, still in the sintering temperature, and left to cool down in the external environment, in the air. Fig. 5 shows the optical microscopy quality of the specimen with 80% Fe and 20% Cr compacted with 800 MPa and sintered in Argon atmosphere (Ar) for 60, 180 and 360 min.Fig. 5Optical microscopy of the sample 80%Fe 20%Cr 800 MPa for a) 60, b)180 and c) 360 min.Fig. 5

steps.title: Perform EDS and XRD analyses
steps.instruction: Analyze the elemental powders (Fe, Cr, Ni) to verify particle morphology, composition, and crystal structure.

substeps.instruction: Conduct Energy Dispersive Spectrometry (EDS) on each powder using a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) to assess morphology and elemental composition.

Perform X‑ray diffraction (XRD) on the powders using a copper anode (λ = 0.15406 nm) and an angular pitch of 2°, then compare the diffraction patterns with the expected peak positions for each element.

steps.title: Weigh and mix powders
steps.instruction: Prepare homogeneous powder mixtures for compaction.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 90 g of each powder composition (Fe, Cr, Ni) to form a batch for a series of tests.
Place the weighed powders into a Y‑type blender and mix for 60 min at 45 rpm to achieve homogeneous dispersion.
Divide the mixed batch into 10 g portions, each to be used as an individual test sample.

steps.title: Compress powders into compacts
steps.instruction: Uniaxially compact each 10 g sample in a steel die following ASTM B925‑15.

substeps.instruction: Use a rigid steel die with an internal diameter of Ø = 18.75 mm and a calibrated press capable of ≥30 tonnes.
Insert the lower punch (smaller) into the die and place the elastic spacer beneath it.
Add the powder into the cavity, then position the upper punch on top.
Place the assembly in the press and apply a 1 t load to support the die and remove the spacer.
Increase the load to the final value at approximately 20 MPa · s⁻¹, keeping the load for no more than 10 s.
Release the pressure, remove the lower punch, insert the upper spacer, and extract the compact.

steps.title: Determine compaction curves
steps.instruction: Measure green density of compacts at various pressures to generate compaction curves for each composition.

substeps.instruction: Compact samples at incremental loads ranging from 700 MPa to 1000 MPa.
For pure Fe, record green density at 700, 800, 900, and 1000 MPa.
For Fe‑Cr mixtures (10 %, 20 %, 30 % Cr), record green density at 800, 900, and 1000 MPa.
Plot density versus applied pressure for each composition to obtain the compaction curve.

steps.title: Sinter compacts in argon furnace
steps.instruction: Heat the compacted samples to 1200 °C in an inert atmosphere and hold for specified times.

substeps.instruction: Identify each compact and place it on an ASTM 304 steel plate (matching chromium content) inside the furnace.
Purge the furnace with argon and maintain a gas flow of 4 L min⁻¹.
Program the furnace to raise the temperature to 1200 °C while the atmosphere remains inert.
Position an auxiliary thermocouple just above the samples; monitor the heating rate with a thermometer of 0.1 °C resolution, referenced to 1200 °C per the calibration certificate.
When 1200 °C is reached, insert the samples (if not already in place).
Hold the temperature for one of the following durations: 60 min, 180 min, or 360 min.
After the hold time, remove the samples while still hot and allow them to cool in ambient air.

steps.title: Conduct post‑sintering SEM/EDS analysis
steps.instruction: Examine the sintered samples for microstructure, porosity, and elemental distribution.

substeps.instruction: Perform scanning electron microscopy (SEM) using back‑scattered electron imaging on each sintered sample.
Acquire energy‑dispersive X‑ray spectroscopy (EDS) maps of the same region to visualize elemental distribution.
Repeat the SEM and EDS procedures for all composition variations, compaction pressures, and sintering times (60, 180, 360 min).
